react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: perturbed galactose metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052) as the top two hits with FDR = 1.43 × 10⁻¹¹ and fold-enrichment > 1,300, implicating four driver metabolites (sucrose, galactitol, myo-inositol, galactinol). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as the top result (p = 3.25 × 10⁻⁷, rank 1). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.024, rank 6) and additionally surfaced Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.021, rank 5) — the latter driven by 16(R)-HETE (CHEBI:34162) and myo-inositol, consistent with the known role of inositol lipids in membrane remodeling. β-alanine appears in the urea-cycle/amino-group metabolism module (MUMM rank 12) and in the RaMP transport pathways, indicating a secondary perturbation of amino-acid handling. The five galactose-axis compounds are structurally resolved with no InChIKey conflicts, and the cross-tool consensus is internally consistent: sucrose (C00089) → galactose → galactitol (C01697) with galactinol (C01235) as the raffinose-family donor; myo-inositol (C00137) closes the inositol pool at the intersection of galactose and glycerophospholipid metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a dominant perturbation of the galactose metabolic axis. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as the top-ranked KEGG hit with FDR = 1.43×10⁻¹¹ and fold-enrichment = 1,394.6; the SMPDB Galactosemia pathway (SMPDB:SMP00182) shared the same rank-0 position, both driven by four input compounds. Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently identified MUMM:hexose_phosphorylation (p = 2.60×10⁻³) and MUMM:galactose_metabolism (p = 2.38×10⁻²) in the top 10, confirming a shared galactose/sugar-phosphate theme. The four driver metabolites are sucrose, galactitol, myo-inositol, and galactinol — all confirmed members of KEGG:map00052 by RaMP annotation. Galactose-1-phosphate adenylyltransferase (EC 2.7.7.12) is the canonical Leloir-pathway enzyme that converts galactose-1-phosphate to UDP-galactose, linking galactitol accumulation to the downstream arm of this pathway. A secondary perturbation of β-alanine transport is supported by RaMP Reactome hits (REACT:R-HSA-425366, R-HSA-425407), though these rank below the galactose axis.

RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052) as the top two hits with FDR = 1.43 × 10⁻¹¹ and fold-enrichment > 1,300, implicating four driver metabolites (sucrose, galactitol, myo-inositol, galactinol). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as the top result (p = 3.25 × 10⁻⁷, rank 1). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.024, rank 6) and additionally surfaced Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.021, rank 5) — the latter driven by 16(R)-HETE (CHEBI:34162) and myo-inositol, consistent with the known role of inositol lipids in membrane remodeling. β-alanine appears in the urea-cycle/amino-group metabolism module (MUMM rank 12) and in the RaMP transport pathways, indicating a secondary perturbation of amino-acid handling. The five galactose-axis compounds are structurally resolved with no InChIKey conflicts, and the cross-tool consensus is internally consistent: sucrose (C00089) → galactose → galactitol (C01697) with galactinol (C01235) as the raffinose-family donor; myo-inositol (C00137) closes the inositol pool at the intersection of galactose and glycerophospholipid metabolism.' rewritten_output='Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: perturbed galactose metabolism.
